newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down on RBI dollar buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down on RBI dollar buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee touched a four-week low of 35.855 on Tuesday on sustained dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), dealers said.
The rupee opened Tuesday at 35.780/785 and closed at 35.830/835, dealers said.
They said the rupee traded at a high of 35.78 and a low of 35.855 on Tuesday, although only stray deals were done at the latter figure.
"Only stray deals were at 35.855, the day's range was basically 35.78 to 35.85," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The RBI bought dollars practically throughout this range."
"We last saw 35.855 on April 11," he said.

The rupee has been on strong ground in recent months on good dollar supply and poor demand and exporters have been asking for a fall in the rupee's value against the dollar to protect their competitiveness in global markets.
However the RBI has been constrained in its efforts to check the rupee's rise by the impact its dollar purchases have on domestic money supply.
The central bank's dollar purchases inject rupees into the banking system which lead to a growth in domestic money supply and stoke inflationary pressures.
But liquidity has tightened since a state government bond issue last week.

An issue of 10-year bonds by 25 state government was heavily over-subscribed with the central bank receiving bids for 53.81 billion rupees. The RBI said it would accept all bids received and details from outlying centres are yet to come in.
The funds outflows squeezed liquidity and boosted call money rates above 9.0 percent on Friday, from sub-1.0 percent levels seen through most of April.

"Given the firming up of call rates, the RBI may have decided to step up its intervention in the forex market," said a dealer. "Earlier it was worried about the effects of its intervention on domestic monetary supply expansion."
Dealers gave varied estimates of the RBI's dollar purchases on Tuesday, ranging from $200 million to $250 million. Monday's purchases by the central bank were put at around $150 million.
The RBI's buying has driven the rupee down from Monday's opening 35.745/755.
Dealers also suggested the RBI may be looking to improve liquidity ahead of a forthcoming bond issue by the federal government.
The RBI auctions 30 billion rupees of five-year federal government bonds on Friday.
"I think they may be trying to improve liquidity and push down call money rates before the auction," said a dealer. "If call remains at 9.0-10.0 percent levels, response to the auction may be poor."
Dealers said the rupee strengthened against the forward dollar on exporter sales, after opening lower.
November delivery dollars ended Tuesday at a premium of 85/87 paise after opening at 92/94.
Dealers said exporters sold forward dollars to take advantage of the higher opening premium.
"Given the higher opening (of forward premiums) and that the rupee weakened in spot, some exporters sold to take advantage of the higher premiums," said a dealer.
"Further there is also improved sentiment in the market as it expects forward premiums to be soft on inproved liquidity in the next couple of days," he said.
